messages:
zoe: Noticed a support case — customers copy our Go quickstart into HTTP handlers and streams don't cancel because the snippet creates the stream with context.Background().

karl: Oof. Quick fix: update the quickstart to pass the request context (r.Context()) or a derived timeout and call `defer gen.Close()` immediately. Note that the client can be long-lived but streaming calls must use a request-scoped ctx.

anya: There's a companion bug in the retry/backoff helper: it uses time.Sleep for jitter which ignores ctx.Done(), so retries can keep goroutines alive. I have a small patch switching to time.NewTimer + select on timer.C and ctx.Done().

karl: Please open PRs for the retry fix and the docs update. Also add a small smoke test that starts a generator, cancels the context, and asserts goroutine count returns to baseline within ~200ms to catch regressions.

ci-bot: CI: build passed on branch fix/go-gen-ctx (job #10021) :white_check_mark:

docs-bot: Docs PR opened to swap the quickstart snippet and add a sidebar: "Prefer request context; avoid context.Background() for streams."

zoe: Thanks — also filing an RFC to standardize stream API names (use Close() across stream types). We'll discuss migration strategy and a compatibility shim for older callers.

anya: Done. Pushed retry patch, smoke test, and linked a tiny sample-app repro in the issue for support to triage.
